events.title: British Surrender at Saratoga
events.description: British General John Burgoyne surrendered approximately 5,800 troops to American General Horatio Gates following the Battles of Saratoga in New York.
events.significance: Often considered the turning point of the American Revolutionary War, the victory convinced France to formally ally with the American colonies, providing crucial military and financial support.

events.title: Thomas Edison Files Patent Caveat for the Motion Picture Camera
events.description: Thomas Edison filed a caveat with the U.S. Patent Office describing a device that would do for the eye what the phonograph did for the ear, an early step toward motion picture technology.
events.significance: This filing launched Edison's work on the Kinetoscope, helping lay the foundation for the motion picture industry.

events.title: Al Capone Convicted of Tax Evasion
events.description: Notorious Chicago gangster Al Capone was found guilty of federal income tax evasion charges and was later sentenced to 11 years in prison.
events.significance: The conviction ended the reign of one of America's most infamous organized crime figures and demonstrated the effectiveness of financial investigations against organized crime.

events.title: Loma Prieta Earthquake Strikes San Francisco Bay Area
events.description: A magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck Northern California just before Game 3 of the World Series, killing 63 people and causing major damage, including the collapse of a section of the Bay Bridge and the Cypress Street Viaduct in Oakland.
events.significance: The disaster prompted major advances in seismic engineering, retrofitting of bridges and buildings, and emergency preparedness in California.

events.title: Mother Teresa Awarded the Nobel Peace Prize
events.description: Mother Teresa was announced as the recipient of the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize for her humanitarian work with the poor and dying in Calcutta, India.
events.significance: The award brought global attention to her Missionaries of Charity and to the plight of the world's poorest people.
